subject: different models for different groups in cross-level cfa?

messages.author: b2879fd01c83afa4
messages.subject: different models for different groups in cross-level cfa?
parts:
Hi guys,

I read the tutorial that 'By default, the same model is fitted in all groups', and I'm wondering whether I can fit different models for different groups? And probably cross-level?

For instance, I have data for nested leader-member data in which several members are nested under one team-leader. I have measures for leaders' job satisfaction and turnover intent; and measures for members job satisfaction and performance. Can I do a cross-level cfa to show that there are four distinct factors? Maybe also by calling some function from lavaan.survey?

I guess models might look something like:

model <- ' leaderJobSat =~ 1 * sat1 + sat2 + sat3
                 leaderTurnover =~ 1 * tover1 + tover2 + tover3 + tover4

                 memberJobSat =~ 1 * sat1 + sat2 + sat3
                 memberPerf =~ 1 * perf1 + perf2 + perf3
        
                group = "leaderOrMember"        '



Tons of thanks! And any help is appreciated.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: different models for different groups in cross-level cfa?
parts:
On 07/14/2015 12:03 AM, Kuochen Chao wrote:
> I read the tutorial that 'By default, the same model is fitted in all
> groups', and I'm wondering whether I can fit different models for
> different groups? And probably cross-level?

Hm. In principle, you can, but this is (currently, 0.5-18) unsupported
and not documented (and incomplete), see:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/lavaan/multiple$20groups$20analysis$20in$20Lavaan/lavaan/0eS49Cmgrew/ocZ-JVFSr6IJ

> For instance, I have data for nested leader-member data in which several
> members are nested under one team-leader. I have measures for leaders'
> job satisfaction and turnover intent; and measures for members job
> satisfaction and performance. Can I do a cross-level cfa to show that
> there are four distinct factors?

Well, it may be possible using the multiple group approach, but that may
be tricky. I have no example script for this.

The ideal solution would be multilevel CFA. lavaan does not do that
(yet). Mplus can do this. And 'gllamm' (a Stata module) too.

> Maybe also by calling some function
> from lavaan.survey?

That would only work if you have data on 'level-1' only. The
lavaan.survey package handles the 'clustering' of your data, but does
not allow you to fit a model at several levels.

Yves.
